_about: The unique combined accessibility checklist: WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA. This is the strict superset of every stable web accessibility requirement the three source checklists point to. Section 508 of 2017 incorporates WCAG 2.0 A and AA by reference; the US ADA via the DOJ Title II rule of 2024 requires WCAG 2.1 AA; WCAG 2.2 contains both. Meeting every item here therefore satisfies 508 and the ADA Title II web standard and exceeds them in practice. The one exception is 4.1.1 Parsing, the single Level A criterion present in WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 but removed in 2.2 (modern browsers and assistive tech handle the duplicate-id and malformed-markup cases it covered), so it is treated as always satisfied rather than listed as its own item; this is why the superset holds in practice. Per-item flags: s508 = also required by Section 508 (a WCAG 2.0 criterion); ada = also required by ADA Title II (a WCAG 2.0 or 2.1 criterion). method: automated = an automated check (axe/lint) fully covers the testable surface; both = automation catches some instances but misses others, so a human must also confirm; manual = no reliable automated detection.
_wcag3_note: WCAG 3.0 is a W3C Working Draft (requirements document, Group Note Draft), not a ratified standard, so no conformance can be claimed to it today. It is tracked as direction only (broader-than-web scope, a conformance model beyond pass/fail, stronger low-vision and cognitive support). This checklist gates to the stable standards; adopt WCAG 3.0 guidance as it matures.
_scope_note: The ADA Checklist for Existing Facilities (adata.org) covers physical buildings, not the web, so it is out of scope for a website gate. For the web, ADA obligations are met through WCAG, which this checklist covers. The WebAIM Section 508 checklist page is self-marked out-of-date; the authoritative mapping used here is that Section 508 incorporates WCAG 2.0 A and AA.
source: Success criteria and plain-language requirements per WCAG 2.2 (w3.org/TR/WCAG22) and WebAIM's current WCAG 2 checklist (webaim.org/standards/wcag/checklist, last updated 2024-06-20). The obsolete 4.1.1 Parsing criterion is excluded. AAA criteria are out of scope for this AA gate.

criteria.name: Non-text Content
criteria.req: Give images and non-text content a text alternative; decorative items get an empty alt.

criteria.name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.req: Transcript for audio-only; transcript or audio track for video-only.

criteria.name: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.req: Recorded video has captions synced to the audio.

criteria.name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.req: Recorded video gives a transcript or audio description for important visuals.

criteria.name: Captions (Live)
criteria.req: Live audio or video has synced captions.

criteria.name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.req: Recorded video with important visuals has audio description.

criteria.name: Info and Relationships
criteria.req: Visual structure (headings, lists, tables, labels, groups) is also coded in markup.

criteria.name: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.req: The reading and focus order follows a logical sequence in the code.

criteria.name: Sensory Characteristics
criteria.req: Instructions do not rely only on shape, size, location, or sound.

criteria.name: Orientation
criteria.req: Content is not locked to portrait or landscape unless essential.

criteria.name: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.req: Fields collecting common personal data use the correct autocomplete value.

criteria.name: Use of Color
criteria.req: Color is not the only means of conveying information or distinguishing elements.

criteria.name: Audio Control
criteria.req: Audio that plays over 3 seconds can be paused, stopped, or muted.

criteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.req: Text contrast at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text); automation misses text in images.

criteria.name: Resize Text
criteria.req: Readable and usable at 200% zoom without loss of content or function.

criteria.name: Images of Text
criteria.req: Use real text rather than images of text, except logos and the essential.

criteria.name: Reflow
criteria.req: Usable at 320 CSS px wide with no two-dimensional scrolling, except data tables and maps.

criteria.name: Non-text Contrast
criteria.req: UI components, states, and graphical objects have at least 3:1 contrast.

criteria.name: Text Spacing
criteria.req: Content still works when users increase line, paragraph, letter, and word spacing.

criteria.name: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.req: Hover and focus pop-ups are dismissable, hoverable, and persistent.

criteria.name: Keyboard
criteria.req: All functionality is operable by keyboard alone.

criteria.name: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.req: Keyboard focus can always move away from any component.

criteria.name: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.req: Single-character shortcuts can be turned off, remapped, or scoped to focus.

criteria.name: Timing Adjustable
criteria.req: Users can turn off, adjust, or extend time limits, with narrow exceptions.

criteria.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.req: Moving, blinking, or auto-updating content over 5 seconds can be paused, stopped, or hidden.

criteria.name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.req: Nothing flashes more than three times per second, or stays under the flash thresholds.

criteria.name: Bypass Blocks
criteria.req: A skip link or landmarks let users bypass repeated blocks of content.

criteria.name: Page Titled
criteria.req: Each page has a descriptive, informative title. Automation can confirm a title is present; a human must confirm it is descriptive.

criteria.name: Focus Order
criteria.req: Keyboard focus moves through content in a meaningful, logical order.

criteria.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.req: Each link's purpose is clear from its text or immediate context.

criteria.name: Multiple Ways
criteria.req: More than one way to find a page (search, site map, navigation).

criteria.name: Headings and Labels
criteria.req: Headings and labels describe their topic or purpose.

criteria.name: Focus Visible
criteria.req: A visible focus indicator shows which element has keyboard focus.

criteria.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.req: A focused element is not entirely hidden by author-created content.

criteria.name: Pointer Gestures
criteria.req: Multipoint or path-based gestures have a single-pointer alternative unless essential.

criteria.name: Pointer Cancellation
criteria.req: Actions do not complete on down-event alone; users can abort or undo.

criteria.name: Label in Name
criteria.req: A control's accessible name contains its visible label text.

criteria.name: Motion Actuation
criteria.req: Motion-operated features have a control alternative and can be disabled.

criteria.name: Dragging Movements
criteria.req: Drag-based functions also work with a single tap or click.

criteria.name: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.req: Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS px, or have equivalent spacing, with exceptions.

criteria.name: Language of Page
criteria.req: The page's default human language is set in the markup.

criteria.name: Language of Parts
criteria.req: Passages in a different language are marked with their language.

criteria.name: On Focus
criteria.req: Moving focus to a component does not trigger an unexpected change of context.

criteria.name: On Input
criteria.req: Changing a setting does not cause an unexpected change of context without warning.

criteria.name: Consistent Navigation
criteria.req: Repeated navigation keeps the same relative order across pages.

criteria.name: Consistent Identification
criteria.req: Components with the same function are identified consistently across pages.

criteria.name: Consistent Help
criteria.req: Help mechanisms appear in the same relative order across pages.

criteria.name: Error Identification
criteria.req: Input errors are identified in text and described to the user.

criteria.name: Labels or Instructions
criteria.req: Form inputs have labels or instructions.

criteria.name: Error Suggestion
criteria.req: When an input error is detected, a correction suggestion is offered if known.

criteria.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
criteria.req: Legal, financial, or data submissions are reversible, checked, or confirmed.

criteria.name: Redundant Entry
criteria.req: Information already entered in the same process is auto-populated or selectable.

criteria.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.req: Login needs no cognitive function test unless an alternative or a mechanism exists.

criteria.name: Name, Role, Value
criteria.req: UI components expose a correct name, role, state, and value to assistive tech.

criteria.name: Status Messages
criteria.req: Status messages are announced by assistive tech without moving focus.
